evals.name: top-vulnerabilities-default-target
evals.prompt: Do a ruthless security audit of the Django app at skills/_fixtures/vuln-app. Find the worst vulnerabilities and prove each one. Do not change your working directory.

assertions.text: Reports between 1 and 3 confirmed findings (respects the stop-early cap)
Surfaces at least one genuine high/critical-severity plant from the ground-truth set (any of S1-S7 counts)
Every finding cites a file:line location
At least one finding includes a real proof: a CVE id for a vulnerable dependency, or a minimal PoC for a novel bug
All reported findings are security issues, not efficiency/performance issues
Does not report the get_product decoy (D1) as a SQL-injection finding

evals.name: decoy-trap-reachability
evals.prompt: Review skills/_fixtures/vuln-app before we ship it and flag the security issues that are actually exploitable. I keep getting scanner reports full of false positives, so only tell me about things a real attacker can actually reach and trigger. Stay in the current directory.

assertions.text: Reports between 1 and 3 confirmed findings (respects the stop-early cap)
Findings are genuinely reachable/exploitable plants (e.g. S1/S2/S3/S4/S6), each with a PoC or CVE
Does NOT report the get_product endpoint (D1) as SQL injection — recognizes the int() cast neutralizes it
For each finding, states who reaches it (unauthenticated vs authenticated) — demonstrating reachability was checked

evals.name: dependency-cve-flavored
evals.prompt: Audit skills/_fixtures/vuln-app for security problems — I'm especially worried our pinned dependencies have known CVEs. Report the top few with proof. Don't cd anywhere.

assertions.text: At least one finding is a known-vulnerable dependency from requirements.txt with a cited CVE id
The cited CVE id maps to the actual package@version pinned (not fabricated)
Every finding cites a file:line or the manifest location
